quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

33 Questions • Passing Score 27

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must always be obeyed.
Are merely suggestions.
Must be followed only when there is other traffic.
Must be followed only when a police officer is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must always be obeyed.
questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and guide drivers safely. You must always obey them.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the interstate, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn into an exit. Continue driving and take the next exit instead.

questions.question: The sign with this shape and color is a ____ sign.

options.text: No passing zone
Wrong way
Railroad crossing
Stop

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs are used only to show a no passing zone.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol socially, what helps ensure safe driving?

options.text: Drink coffee before driving.
Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.
Stop drinking one half hour before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid driving while impaired is to get a ride from a friend who has not been drinking. Coffee and cold showers do not reduce alcohol effects. Your body takes about one hour to eliminate alcohol from one drink.

questions.question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving:

options.text: Are always aware of the risks they are taking.
Cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles properly.
Are better drivers because they are more careful than sober drivers.
Have quicker reaction times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol damages judgment, vision, focus, and reaction time. It is never safe to drink any amount of alcohol before driving.

questions.question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is true?

options.text: Never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
Airbags can harm an infant or small child, even in a slow crash.
Always make sure all passengers use a seat belt or child restraint.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before driving, fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce your chance of injury or death in a crash. Children age 12 and under should sit properly restrained in the rear seat. Never put a rear-facing infant seat in the front seat of a vehicle with a front airbag.

questions.question: When driving on slick roads, you should:

options.text: Take turns more slowly than usual.
Change lanes quickly.
Accelerate quickly.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take turns more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast on slippery roads is dangerous, especially in turns and curves. Slow down more than you normally would when the road is slippery.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:

options.text: Stop immediately.
Help the injured.
Call the police.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. If possible, move it out of traffic. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people unless necessary, but help stop severe bleeding with direct pressure. Wait for emergency vehicles.

questions.question: If you are in a serious motor vehicle crash, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Call the police.
Check if anyone is injured.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Move your vehicle off the road and stop if possible. If anyone is hurt, call 911 and help them. You must report the crash to police if there is an injury, death, or more than $1,000 in property damage (or more than $200 in damage to government property like signs or guardrails).

questions.question: Drivers who eat and drink while driving:

options.text: Make no driving errors.
Have trouble driving slowly.
Are better drivers because they are not hungry.
Have trouble controlling their vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have trouble controlling their vehicles.
questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous because it takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. These distractions make it hard to stay in your lane and control your vehicle.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always use your signal, even if you don't see other cars.
Signal only if other cars are visible.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only when driving in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use your signal, even if you don't see other cars.
questions.explanation: Always use your signal when changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from a curb. Do not skip signaling—it is a law and an important safety habit.

questions.question: If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, you must:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Wait until the train completely passes before crossing.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find another route to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the train completely passes before crossing.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is close or moving fast, do not cross. This applies even if there are no signals or if the signals are broken.

questions.question: At a four-way stop:

options.text: The driver who arrived first goes first.
The driver who arrived last goes first.
One driver should keep going without stopping.
One driver should wave the others ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrived first goes first.
questions.explanation: All four drivers must stop at a four-way stop. The driver who reaches the intersection first has the right to go first. If two cars arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: Before turning, you should:

options.text: Use your signal.
Turn the wheel.
Speed up.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your signal.
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:

options.text: Cars already in the roundabout.
Bicyclists in the roundabout.
Pedestrians in the roundabout.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to all pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in it.

questions.question: You should slow down:

options.text: On narrow or winding roads.
At intersections and railroad crossings.
When roads are wet or slippery.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections, near railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp curves, where there are pedestrians, near hazards, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Brake hard right away.
Keep the wheel straight and slowly take your foot off the gas.
Keep your speed the same and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to warn cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel straight and slowly take your foot off the gas.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tight and keep the car straight. Take your foot off the gas slowly. Do not brake until you have control. Once the car is steady, brake gently and pull over safely.

questions.question: You see a driver ahead using one hand and talking to a passenger. You should:

options.text: Give that car extra space.
Know that inattentive driving increases accident risk.
Not copy their driving habits.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted while driving by passengers, searching the car, reading, sightseeing, or daydreaming. If another driver looks distracted, give them extra space because accidents are more likely.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Steep downgrade ahead.
Crossroad ahead.
No right turn.
Narrow bridge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and tell drivers about upcoming hazards. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Adjust your speed to avoid brake problems or crashes.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is nearby, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get out of the way.
Stop immediately and block their path.
Do everything you can to clear a path for them.
Signal to them when it is safe to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do everything you can to clear a path for them.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near, give them a clear path. If safe, pull to the side of the road so they can pass.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Signal before you change lanes.
Check your blind spot.
Make sure the lane is clear.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes or exiting. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving left or right.

questions.question: Before starting the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure only backseat passengers are buckled.
Make sure only adult passengers are buckled.
Make sure only children are buckled.
Make sure everyone in the car is buckled.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure everyone in the car is buckled.
questions.explanation: Before starting the car, buckle your seat belt. Make sure all passengers buckle theirs too.

questions.question: To cross a railroad safely, you should:

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.
Listen and look both ways before crossing if it is safe.
Cross quickly when a train is approaching.
Quickly go under the lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen and look both ways before crossing if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are dangerous. Always look and listen for trains from both directions before crossing. Watch for signals and never cross unless you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: What is the correct way to change lanes?

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Signal in the direction you want to move. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure the far lane is clear. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol while taking drugs can:

options.text: Decrease the effects of drugs and alcohol.
Increase the effects of both drugs and alcohol.
Help cure your illness.
Improve your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the effects of both drugs and alcohol.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs can increase the effects of both. It is unsafe to drive after using either one. It is even more dangerous to use them together.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?

options.text: Look in the left side mirror.
Look in the right side mirror.
Look in the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot, look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.question: What do highway markings do?

options.text: They are usually not important.
They are only found in construction zones.
They provide information for drivers.
They are usually red and blue.

questions.correctAnswerText: They provide information for drivers.
questions.explanation: Highway markings help drivers position their vehicles correctly. They show safe passing zones and warn drivers about upcoming conditions.

questions.question: When stopped by police, you must show:

options.text: Proof of insurance.
Your driver's license.
Proof of registration.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must have and show your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance. These three documents are required in your vehicle.

questions.question: Two solid white lines mark a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know:

options.text: Cars have the right-of-way over pedestrians.
Pedestrians in the crosswalk have the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in the crosswalk have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show where pedestrians can safely cross. You must always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Side road.
Low clearance.
Merging traffic.
Prepare to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Side road.
questions.explanation: This is a warning sign. It is usually yellow with black markings. It warns you that traffic may enter from a nearby side road.

questions.question: What does a yellow and black diamond-shaped sign mean?

options.text: It warns you about road conditions ahead or nearby.
It helps you find cities and towns.
It tells you about traffic laws and rules.
It tells you about road construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: It warns you about road conditions ahead or nearby.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with yellow backgrounds and black symbols or words. They alert you to conditions on or near the road ahead.

questions.question: What should you do to drive safely at night?

options.text: Stay farther away from other cars.
Do not drive if you feel tired.
Check that your headlights work properly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as well. Do all these things to keep yourself and other drivers safe in the dark.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is correct?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can kill.
Speeding is safe if you are a good driver.
Both driving too slowly on certain highways and speeding are dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both driving too slowly on certain highways and speeding are dangerous.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the risk of death in a crash. At speeds over 80 miles per hour, survival is very unlikely. Driving much slower than other traffic is also dangerous because other drivers may make unsafe moves to pass you.
